recipes.name: Rockin' Salsa
ingredients_raw: 6 pounds fresh tomatoes, peeled and chopped
8 pint canning jars with lids and rings

steps.text: Combine red onion, white onion, yellow onion, tomatoes, banana peppers, green peppers, tomato paste, white vinegar, garlic powder, salt, cayenne pepper, cumin, brown sugar, and white sugar in a large pot. Simmer until thick, about 3 hours.

Sterilize the jars and lids in boiling water for at least 5 minutes. Pack the salsa into the hot, sterilized jars, filling the jars to within 1/4 inch of the top. Run a knife or a thin spatula around the insides of the jars after they have been filled to remove any air bubbles. Wipe the rims of the jars with a moist paper towel to remove any food residue. Top with lids, and screw on rings.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then carefully lower the jars into the pot using a holder. Leave a 2 inch space between the jars. Pour in more boiling water if necessary until the water level is at least 1 inch above the tops of the jars. Bring the water to a full boil, cover the pot, and process for 10 to 15 minutes.

Remove the jars from the stockpot and place onto a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, until cool. Once cool, press the top of each lid with a finger, ensuring that the seal is tight (lid does not move up or down at all). Refrigerate after opening.

raw_recipe.headline: Rockin' Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This recipe makes several jars of spicy salsa that's great for gift-giving or to just have in your pantry.

review.reviewBody: 3 stars as written, 5 stars with minor alterations. I took the advice of others, and cut the sugar in half, and it was still too tad sweet for my taste. Tried to remedy with about 3 T. bottled lime juice, but still a bit sweet. Sugar should be omitted, but the lime is a nice addition. The heat of the salsa (somewhere between mild and medium) is good, but I like a little more kick. In subsequent batches, I adjusted the ingredients more to my liking, being mindful of the acid / non-acid ingredient ratios for safety reasons. The addition of the lime juice allowed me to use 5-6 cloves of fresh minced garlic (instead of garlic powder) and 2 T. of freshly minced cilantro. I stuck with the 3 cups of mixed onions, but played with the peppers. Keeping the total amount at about 2 1/2 cups, I used 4 jalapenos, 2 banana peppers, and then 2 green bells. I also upped the cumin to 2 tsp. Cooking for 3 hours is ridiculous... to do so would leave you with no texture to your salsa at all! After chopping all the veg, I placed them in a colander over a bowl for an hour to drain excess moisture. When I mixed all the ingredients in the pot, I boiled for about 15-20 minutes, which is plenty long enough for safety issues.

I have made this recipe 4 times now this season. It is excellent! I made it exactly as the recipe said. The next time I added cauliflowerettes for added crunch. Today I added 2 jalapeños because my guy wanted to pump it up a notch or two. The type of tomatoes I grew were very juicy so I cooked them down a bit and strained the juice out. Keeping that for a soup base. I serve this in a bowl that has sour cream to one side and then pour the salsa on the other side.

I made only half a batch - 3.5lbs of tomatoes (Celebrity and Rutgers mix) because I expected NOT to like it. It was AMAZING! Used 1 green pepper, 2 jalapenos (one with seed, one without) and one pepper that I have no idea what it was. It looked like a banana pepper but was much bigger...about 6" long. No label on it at the grocers...someone said it was a "Hatch" pepper. I de-seeded it too. Used just over 2 cups of onion...red, yellow and white. Used 1 1/2 cans of tomato paste and 1/4 cup white vinegar, then the seasonings as per the recipe but added some oregano. DID NOT USE ANY SUGAR! And I don't think I would have like it if I did! This still filled up my Dutch oven to the 1/2 way mark so still made quite a bit. DEFINITELY will make again with all the ripe tomatoes I cannot use!

I really like this recipe.....the heat and sweet acidity . Now I did change two things......I halved the sugar and I used a stick blender when the salsa finished cooking to create more of picanti style salsa. I'm not a lover of chunky salsa, but there are plenty chunky salsa lovers out there. I caned half what I made then gave away to friends half what I kept. My friends loved it so much they finished the 2 cups of salsa shortly after I gave it to them. The heat builds as you eat this salsa, that's perfect for what I would call a low medium heat salsa.

I’ve made this salsa for the past 3 summers with our garden tomatoes, peppers and onions, great recipe but I’ve tweaked it to suit our tastes. I only used a few table spoons of sugar & use about 4 fresh jalapeños with 1 habenero instead of banana peppers and eliminate the cayenne. I also use a stick blender after simmering for a more smooth consistency

I'm only rating four because I did make some changes. This recipe is a lot of effort, but you get lots of salsa. I followed other peoples advice and reduced the sugar. I didn't want to omit it because I've heard that sugar changes the flavour of tomatoes, but I've had good, sweet salsa before and thought it would have been great salsa if it wasn't so sweet. I also like it hot, so instead of 2 banana peppers and 3 green peppers I added 3 jalapeños, 6 serrano and 2 sweet peppers (I didn't have green peppers, so I used 1 orange and 1 yellow). I also simmered the salsa with 5 whole serrano peppers and removed them when complete. Simmered the salsa for at least two hours.

This is our main salsa recipe and everyone we share it with loves it. We start with the basic recipe but substitute yellow, red and orange peppers for all but one of the green peppers. We also add one jalapeño and one Serrano pepper instead of the banana pepper. For tomatoes, we use only Romas and they are fantastic in this recipe. No change in seasonings, but we hold on the sugars because the colored peppers are sweet enough. Cooking only for 1 to 1 1/2 hours at most before canning. I recommend cooling down some for taste testing before canning - just in case you need to add anything more!! Great recipe!!!

Turned out to be a very fresh and delicious salsa that my family loved! I followed the recipe except I also added 1/2 cup of fresh lemon juice, 2 jalapeños, seeds removed and chopped, 1-1/2 tsp oregano and 1-1/2 tsp parsley. Also, I boiled the mixture for only 15 minutes instead of the recommended 3 hours.

I made some substitutions to suit our taste. I was trying to imitate a pineapple salsa I love. I did not use the banana peppers or crushed red peppers. I added 1 can crushed pineapple and 1 can chunk pineapple but drain the juice. I also added 4 jalapeños (seeds and all) plus one habanero pepper (seeds and all). I substituted the garlic powder for 3 really big garlic cloves minced. My family loves it. It is has a little heat and is super flavorful. It is not super hot, trust me

Turned out great! I must confess I changed it up slightly, just to suit our preferences of bold flavors. Added 6 heads of fresh garlic and some seasoned pepper. I also am adding a note on my canning label recommending that fresh jalapeños and cilantro is added, to taste. Overall a great recipe, love that the onions are still fairly crisp and the flavors are so well blended together.

1st time canning anything and I ROCKED the Rockin Salsa! Neighbor gave me 3# tomatoes and a large quantity of a mix of jalapenos, serranos and banana peppers so I adjusted the recipe to 1/2. After seeing reviews, cut the sugar to 1T mix of white and brown sugar, used 11 of the pepper mix, no bell pepper and added cilantro for last 15 mins. Had hubby taste after 1 hour 15 mins and texture/heat was perfect. Water bath for 15 mins for my altitude (2250). 4 pint jars of heaven. Thank you!

This is my absolute go-to salsa recipe! I’ve been making it for years since I first saw the recipe. I will not make any other recipe for salsa because it’s beyond good and I get nothing but raves from my family and friends (especially my husband!). You won’t be disappointed making this.

I love the recipe, and not a fan of spicy foods, but my family and friends love it, so I make it for them. Friends parents were visiting recently from Japan, they loved the Salsa and took some jars back home with them, to Japan.
Best salsa ever! Makes the house smell amazing and everyone that tries it raves over it!
I have been making this exact same recipe for over 10 years. Give credit where credit is due!

Perfect recipe for those who like thicker salsa. I make it every fall with my sister-about 100 lbs of Romas tomatoes. We give it away to our kids and friends around Christmas. So yummy. Each batch we change the pepper concentration and label. This is my 4th year making this recipe. It’s a keeper.
I made this as is, just doubled the recipe and put into quarts. Favorite salsa recipe!

I was introduced to this recipe by my son years ago and loved it so much I started making it from veggies from my garden and give as gifts to my friends. We all love it. I do add extra hot peppers in some batches to make it for those who love it spicy.
